look.text: A weathered stone shrine with a basin and a single candle stub. Folk used to leave candles here for the sick; there's only one now, and it's guttering.

choices.text: Read the inscription on the basin.

pray.text: You say the old words. Nothing answers: no warmth, no stillness, nothing. Whatever used to listen here has stopped, or has been drawn away.

choices.text: Read the inscription on the basin.
(Acolyte) Say the rite for a silent shrine.

acolyte.text: You know this one: when a shrine goes quiet, it has given more light than it was given. It must be fed. The rite says: "light given freely". Not oil. Something living, that shines.

inscription.text: Worn letters around the basin: "LIGHT GIVEN FREELY KEEPS THE LIGHT". Someone has scratched a little picture under it: a wisp, drifting into the basin.

offer.text: You tip the essence into the basin. It doesn't spill: it rises, and settles into the candle, and the flame stands up straight and bright for the first time in weeks.
